newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says it downed Indian helicopter.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says it downed Indian helicopter.

text.p: Pakistani troops shot down an Indian military helicopter near the ceasefire line in Azad (free) Kashmir last week, a defence source said on Tuesday.

"The (Indian) helicopter carrying five or six people was shot down on Thursday after it did not heed warning shots," said the source. He said the helicopter had violated Pakistani airspace, but did not say where it had been shot down.
Indian officials were not immediately available to comment.

The source said tension had heightened along the Line of Control dividing Kashmir in the run-up to this month's planned state assembly elections in the Indian-ruled part of the Himalayan region. Pakistan has denounced the polls.

Pakistani commanders told reporters on Monday that Indian planes had been flying over the Line of Control for the past week and one even flew over the Siachen Glacier frontline, where planes have rarely been used in the past, on Sunday.
Pakistani and Indian troops face each other along a high-altitude 117-km (73-mile) frontier in the Siachen area, an undemarcated extension of the Line of Control.
Pakistan and India have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over Kashmir.
